title: The Iterable Interface & The Enhanced for-each Loop
summary: How the compiler translates for-each loops into iterator(), hasNext(), and next(), and implementing Iterable on custom domain classes.
learningObjectives: Understand the formal contract of java.lang.Iterable<T> and its role as the root of the Collection hierarchy
Trace javac compiler de-sugaring of enhanced for-each loops into bytecode iterator operations
Implement Iterable<T> and custom Iterator<T> on domain business entities
Differentiate when for-each iteration is appropriate versus when an explicit Iterator reference is mandatory
expectedOutcomes: Ability to explain the mechanics of the enhanced for-each loop in placement interviews
Confidence creating custom domain data structures that integrate seamlessly with standard Java loops

activities.title: Practical Context: Turntable Carousel Luggage Retrieval

analogy.headline: Practical Context: Turntable Carousel Luggage Retrieval
analogy.story:
At an airport baggage claim, luggage arrives on a revolving carousel. The carousel itself does not expose its internal gears, motors, or electrical wiring. Instead, it presents a simple mechanical interface: suitcases emerge sequentially one after another.

You do not need to know whether the conveyor belt is driven by a chain or a hydraulic rotor. You simply stand at the pickup point, observe whether the next suitcase is arriving (`hasNext()`), and pick it up (`next()`).

The `Iterable` interface serves as this exact consumer contract: any object implementing `Iterable` promises to supply a sequential stream of items on demand.
analogy.keyTakeaway: Iterable defines the universal capability of an object to produce an Iterator. It allows any custom data structure to be traversed using Java's clean for-each loop.

activities.title: The Iterable Contract & Compiler De-Sugaring Mechanics

keyTakeaways: java.lang.Iterable<T> is the superinterface of java.util.Collection<E>
Any class implementing Iterable<T> can be traversed directly using Java's enhanced for-each loop
The compiler transforms for-each loops into while (iterator.hasNext()) { Object x = iterator.next(); }
Implementing custom Iterable requires returning a compliant java.util.Iterator<T> instance
Enhanced for-each loops cannot mutate the collection (remove elements) during traversal

activities.title: Custom Integer Range Generator
activities.description: Trace a lightweight, memory-efficient Integer range generator implementing Iterable<Integer>.

steps.description: IntRange implements Iterable<Integer>. It stores start and end bounds without creating any array in memory.
iterator() returns an anonymous Iterator<Integer>. hasNext() evaluates current <= end; next() returns current and increments.
The for-each loop consumes the range cleanly. Zero array allocation overhead, executing with O(1) memory.

questions.question: What interface must a Java class implement in order to be used as the target of an enhanced for-each loop?
questions.explanation: In Java, any class that implements java.lang.Iterable (or an array) can be used as the target of the enhanced for-each loop.

questions.question: Why can you not remove elements from a collection during an enhanced for-each loop?
options: Because for-each loops only work on immutable arrays
Because the underlying Iterator instance created by the compiler is anonymous and cannot be referenced to call iterator.remove()
Because Java collections do not support removal
Because for-each executes on a background daemon thread
questions.explanation: The compiler creates a hidden synthetic Iterator variable to drive the loop. Because you do not have a reference to this synthetic iterator, you cannot call it.remove(). Calling collection.remove() directly triggers ConcurrentModificationException.

activities.title: Senior Engineer Interview: Iterable vs Iterator

qaList.question: What is the difference between java.lang.Iterable and java.util.Iterator, and why does a collection not implement Iterator directly?
qaList.answer:
Iterable represents an aggregation that CAN BE iterated over (it has an 'iterator()' factory method). Iterator represents the STATE of an in-flight traversal (it maintains the cursor, with 'hasNext()', 'next()', and 'remove()').

If a collection implemented Iterator directly, it could only maintain ONE active cursor at a time. Two nested loops iterating over the same collection ('for (x : c) for (y : c)') or two concurrent threads reading the collection would overwrite each other's cursor position. By separating Iterable (the data container) from Iterator (the independent cursor state), multiple consumers can traverse the same collection simultaneously and independently.

activities.title: Self-Evaluation Checklist
checklist: I understand the difference between Iterable (the container) and Iterator (the traversal cursor)
I can explain how javac de-sugars for-each loops into while (it.hasNext())
I know how to implement Iterable<T> and Iterator<T> on custom domain classes
I understand why calling collection.remove() inside a for-each loop fails

practiceProblems.title: Step-Aware Custom Integer Range
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a class SteppedRange that implements Iterable<Integer>. The constructor takes start, end, and step. The iterator must yield numbers from start to end stepping by step.

practiceProblems.title: Iterable String Word Tokenizer
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a class SentenceWords implementing Iterable<String> that splits a given sentence by whitespace and allows for-each traversal over the words.

practiceProblems.title: Predicate Filtered Iterable Wrapper
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a generic class FilteredIterable<T> that wraps an Iterable<T> and a Predicate<T>. It must only yield elements that satisfy the predicate.

practiceProblems.title: Reverse Array Iterable
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a generic class ReverseArrayIterable<T> that wraps an array T[] and iterates through its elements from the last index down to index 0.

practiceProblems.title: Dual-List Composite Concatenation Iterable
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a class CompositeIterable<T> that takes two Iterable<T> sources and iterates through all elements of the first source followed by all elements of the second source.
